items.title: Efficacy
items.text: Share losing ≥5% by 3 to 6 months. Under 5%, consider stopping

items.title: Safety
items.text: Serious events such as pancreatitis. Stops for side effects. Lean mass loss over 5%

items.title: Adherence
items.text: Still treated at six months. Follow-up visits kept

footnote: Source: Chinese Pharmaceutical Association draft (June 2026), China obesity guideline (2024), ClinicalTrials.gov. AI illustration
notes: We would track three groups of measures, taken from the quality indicators in the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association's draft standard. Efficacy: the share of patients losing at least 5% after 3 to 6 months at the highest tolerated dose, and HbA1c control in patients with diabetes. China's obesity guideline says drug treatment that does not achieve at least 5% weight loss should be stopped. Safety: serious adverse events such as acute pancreatitis, severe allergy and cholecystitis, the share stopping for side effects, and the share losing more than 5% of baseline lean mass. Adherence: the share still treated at six months and the clinic follow-up rate. About two in three US patients stop within a year, so this one needs watching. We would review the program six months after launch. Three outside events could change today's judgment: Novo Nordisk says semaglutide's data protection runs to April 2027, after which domestic generics may be approved. Tirzepatide's outcome trial, SURMOUNT-MMO, is expected to finish in October 2027. And the reimbursement agreements for both drugs run to December 31, 2027.
